s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neck pain with radiating symptoms to the left hand and associated neurological deficits
salient_findings: Electrical pain radiating to the left hand
Weakness in fine movements and weak grip of the left hand
Atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles of the left hand
key_facts: 6-month history of progressive neck pain
Pain radiates to the left hand
Numbness in the C8–T1 dermatomes
Weakness in fine movements of the left hand
Weak grip of the left hand
Atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles of the left hand
Motor testing of the left hand revealed muscle strength of 3/5
Marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra on CT
Lesion involves the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments
Lesion does not significantly compromise the thecal sac

shortlist.label: Osteolytic metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neck pain with radiating symptoms and osteolysis on CT

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Midline location and involvement of anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra with soft tissue component

shortlist.label: Plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Osteolytic lesion with possible neurological deficits

shortlist.label: Spinal tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neck pain with radiating symptoms and possible vertebral collapse

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of progressive neck pain radiating to the left hand, numbness in the C8–T1 dermatomes, and marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra on CT are consistent with osteolytic metastasis. The lesion's involvement of the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments and its heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Chordomas are typically midline and slow-growing, which does not match the patient's rapid progression of symptoms

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Giant cell tumors are usually seen in the epiphyses of long bones and are less likely to cause osteolysis and collapse of the vertebra

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: Plasmacytomas are typically seen in older adults and are less likely to cause marked osteolysis and collapse of the vertebra

rejected.label: Spinal tuberculosis
rejected.why: Spinal tuberculosis typically presents with destruction of the intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebrae, which is not seen in this patient
